title: Foundations: Garage Rock - The Complete Guide
summary: What Garage Rock is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Garage Rock songs: Garage rock is punk before punk: three chords, cheap guitars, and teenage attitude recorded in actual garages. Raw, fast, and gloriously sloppy.

History: The Kingsmen's Louie Louie (1963), the Sonics, the Seeds, and ? and the Mysterians defined the 1960s garage sound; the White Stripes and the Strokes revived it in the 2000s.

How the songs work: Garage Rock favors the keys of E, A, G. Common forms include Two minutes, verse-chorus, done; Fuzz-drenched instrumental break. Players should master maximum fuzz, minimum finesse first, then farisa organ stabs. No capos; cheap guitars in standard.

title: Louie Louie - Garage Rock Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for Louie Louie by The Kingsmen (1963).
body:
Louie Louie — The Kingsmen, 1963. Three chords; investigated by the FBI for alleged obscenity.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of G):
Gm | F | Gm | A#

This study chart uses the 'Fuzz riff i–VII' progression, the Garage Rock workhorse, to map how songs like this move. Form: two minutes, verse-chorus, done. Listen for shouted group vocals — it is the fingerprint of the style.

TO PLAY IT: set your tempo to the Garage Rock pocket, voice the chords cleanly, and let shouted group vocals. No capos; cheap guitars in standard. (Song facts: title/artist/year are documented public records; the chart is an original study arrangement.)
